semantic_baseline_candidates.label: adenine and adenosine salvage III
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: The complete four-reaction route salvages adenine through adenosine, inosine and hypoxanthine to IMP in Escherichia coli K-12. The DeoD homohexamer forms adenosine from adenine and alpha-D-ribose 1-phosphate, Add deaminates adenosine, and DeoD then cleaves inosine. The Hpt homotetramer preferentially salvages hypoxanthine to IMP; Gpt also catalyzes this step with lower affinity for hypoxanthine than for its preferred guanine substrate. Historical genetic experiments used K-12 derivatives, while the native MetaCyc organism annotation is MG1655 and the reviewed proteins are assigned to K-12. The reversible phosphorylase reactions are oriented along the defined salvage route, without claiming that this flux dominates every growth condition. The graph ends at IMP; downstream AMP/GMP synthesis, direct AMP salvage and inosine kinase salvage are separate routes.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: adenosine deoxyribonucleotides de novo biosynthesis II
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: Adenosine deoxyribonucleotide biosynthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C reduces ADP to dADP through the represented ribonucleoside-diphosphate reductase complexes and phosphorylates dADP to dATP through YNK1. The imported formate-dependent ATP-to-dATP branch has no yeast enzyme assignment and is excluded: it describes class III anaerobic ribonucleotide reductase chemistry, whereas the independently characterized yeast system reduces ribonucleoside diphosphates.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: adenosine ribonucleotides de novo biosynthesis
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: Adenosine ribonucleotides de novo biosynthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C converts IMP to adenylo-succinate through ADE12-catalyzed adenylosuccinate synthase activity, cleaves adenylo-succinate to AMP through ADE13-catalyzed adenylosuccinate lyase activity, and phosphorylates AMP to ADP through ADK2- or ADK1-catalyzed AMP kinase activity.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: assimilatory sulfate reduction I
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C assimilatory sulfate reduction route that converts sulfate to hydrogen sulfide through adenosine 5'-phosphosulfate, 3'-phosphoadenylyl-sulfate, and sulfite.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: methionine salvage pathway
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: The methionine salvage pathway in Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C recycles 5'-methylthioadenosine through methylthioribose phosphate, 4-methylthio-2-oxobutanoate, and L-methionine using the SGD GO-CAM MTA salvage reactions.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: NAD salvage pathway V
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: NAD salvage pathway V in Saccharomyces cerevisiae converts nicotinamide through nicotinate, beta-nicotinate D-ribonucleotide, and nicotinate adenine dinucleotide to regenerate NAD in the WP171 GPML diagram.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: periplasmic NAD degradation
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: Periplasmic NAD degradation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C hydrolyzes NAD to AMP and NMN, then dephosphorylates AMP to adenosine and hydrogenphosphate.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: pseudouridine degradation
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: The complete two-step pseudouridine degradation pathway phosphorylates free pseudouridine using ATP, then cleaves its C-C glycosidic bond to uracil and D-ribofuranose 5-phosphate. It follows MetaCyc PWY-6019 and both reactions of the misleadingly titled PathBank Purine Degradation map. The selected protein core is E. coli K-12, supported by reviewed annotations and direct K-12 PsuG characterization. Whole-cell utilization in the original study was in UTI89; kinase structural studies used strain B/BL21 and are not relabeled as K-12 flux or assembly experiments. PsuG is a supported homotrimer. The K-12 kinase is assigned by reviewed functional annotation; the cited dimer experiments concern strain B/BL21, so these sources do not establish the K-12 oligomeric state. Physiological PsuG cleavage is selected despite reversible chemistry and an equilibrium favoring synthesis. Its Mn, Fe and Co alternatives are retained without asserting simultaneous occupancy. The pathway ends at the two cleavage products; RNA pseudouridylation, transport, uracil salvage and downstream pyrimidine-ring degradation are outside the native boundary.

semantic_baseline_candidates.label: Purine Deoxyribonucleosides Degradation
semantic_baseline_candidates.description: The complete six-reaction PathBank pathway annotated here for Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 channels deoxyadenosine, deoxyinosine and deoxyguanosine into free purine bases, acetaldehyde and D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate. Add deaminates deoxyadenosine to deoxyinosine; the DeoD homohexamer provides three parallel phosphorolysis branches, including direct deoxyadenosine cleavage. DeoB transfers the deoxyribose phosphate from C1 to C5 and DeoC cleaves the resulting sugar phosphate. Degradation-directed Rhea reactions retain every chemical side and its exact charge and stereochemistry. This native boundary ends before acetaldehyde oxidation to acetyl-CoA and does not assert purine ring degradation, nucleoside uptake, or nucleotide salvage. MG1655 follows native component annotations; the reviewed proteins are K-12 entries, and the inspected enzyme studies do not establish whole-pathway flux in MG1655. DeoC's monomer/dimer states and Add's inferred zinc assignment remain explicitly qualified.

comparisons.MetaCyc:PWY-6609: Complete 4-step adenine→adenosine→inosine→hypoxanthine→IMP; first shared reaction runs in the opposite selected direction. No Apt/AMP-forming step.
comparisons.PathBank:SMP0002079: Purine deoxyribonucleoside degradation uses different (deoxy) nucleosides and products; no Apt/AMP step.
comparisons.MetaCyc:PWY-6579: Guanosine/guanine GMP salvage has different purine identity and Gpt/Gsk branches.
comparisons.gomodel:YeastPathways_PWY-7219: De novo adenosine ribonucleotide biosynthesis is not adenosine/adenine salvage; yeast context.
comparisons.MetaCyc:P121-PWY: Exact 2-step native route absent from baseline; this authored target is the first maintained instance, not evidence of a pre-existing duplicate.

prior_dispositions: Previous next-189 source dossier explicitly distinguished P121-PWY and PWY-6611 as different variants; it did not add either.
PathBank PW002069/SMP0002081 legacy I is current MetaCyc PWY6609 III.
PathBank PW002071/SMP0002083 legacy II has ADENPHOSPHOR+ADENODEAMIN+INOSINEKIN, matching PWY6611 V biochemical core, not P121.
PathBank PW002072/SMP0002084 legacy III contains adenosine hydrolysis + Apt + AMP hydrolysis and transports; not P121 phosphorolysis.
decision: One distinct complete native P121-PWY record; no claim of pathway inventory exhaustion.
